name: socket-proxy
description: A lightweight, secure-by-default proxy for the Docker socket. Containers that need to read Docker (Traefik, Dozzle, Homepage, Telegraf, n8n) connect to this proxy over TCP instead of mounting /var/run/docker.sock themselves, and the proxy only passes through the exact API calls you allow. Everything is denied until you allow it: set "Allowed Clients" and at least the GET allowlist below, or no client will get through. Allowlists are Go regular expressions, one per HTTP method (a leading ^ and trailing $ are added for you). How other containers use it: put them on the same custom Docker network as this container (name lookup does not work on the default bridge), remove their docker.sock mount, and point them at http://socket-proxy:2375 (for example DOCKER_HOST=tcp://socket-proxy:2375). Do not publish the port to your LAN and never expose it to the internet. Traefik 2.11.31 / 3.6.1 and later also need HEAD /_ping allowed. Coming from the Tecnativa or LinuxServer docker-socket-proxy? The converter at https://socket-proxy-configurator.wollomatic.dev/ turns their environment variables into allowlists. This template runs the container as root (Extra Parameters: --user 0:0) because the image's default user (65534) cannot open the root-owned Docker socket on Unraid. It is also run read-only with all capabilities dropped. For least privilege, check the socket's group with ls -l /var/run/docker.sock and use --user 65534:that group id instead.

paths.name: Docker Socket
paths.description: Host Docker socket the proxy filters. Mounted read-only; the API filtering is done by the allowlists below, not by this mount mode.

variables.name: Allowed Clients
variables.description: Container names or IPs/CIDRs allowed to connect, comma-separated with NO spaces, and each name exactly as Docker shows it (docker ps). Examples: traefik,dozzle or 172.18.0.0/16. A space or a wrong name makes the proxy refuse that client (log: error looking up allowed client hostname). Required: the default only allows localhost, so nothing else could connect.

variables.name: Allow GET
variables.description: Regex of allowed GET paths. Traefik example: /v1\..{1,2}/(version|containers/.*|events.*) . Log and container reading only: /(v1\..{1,2}/)?containers/(json|[^/]+/logs)

variables.name: Allow HEAD
variables.description: Regex of allowed HEAD paths. Traefik 2.11.31 / 3.6.1 and later need /_ping. Leave empty if the client does not use HEAD.

variables.name: Allow POST
variables.description: Regex of allowed POST paths. Leave empty to keep the proxy read-only. POST can start, stop, create and exec containers, so only allow exactly what a trusted client needs (for example a restart-only proxy: /containers/[^/]+/restart).

variables.name: Listen IP
variables.description: Address the proxy binds inside the container. Must be 0.0.0.0 for other containers to reach it.

variables.name: Proxy Port
variables.description: TCP port the proxy listens on inside the container. Not published to the host by this template.

variables.name: Log Level
variables.description: DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR. DEBUG logs every request, which is the easy way to find out which API calls a client needs.

variables.name: Watchdog Interval
variables.description: Check every N seconds that the Docker socket still answers (0 disables). Useful after a Docker engine update.

variables.name: Stop On Watchdog
variables.description: Stop the container when the watchdog finds the socket unavailable, so the restart policy brings it back with a fresh connection.

variables.name: Allowed Bind Mounts
variables.description: Optional, comma-separated host directories that clients may bind-mount in container-create requests, for example /mnt/user/appdata. Only matters if you allow POST.

variables.name: Proxy Container Name
variables.description: Optional. Set to this container's own name to read per-client allowlists from Docker labels (socket-proxy.allow.get and so on) on each client container instead of one global list.
